replacements.instruction: Clarify Table 6 so the cycle-compliance classification forms a 100% partition, the conditional one-pass rate is explicit, and replanning and goal-replacement rates are identified as non-exclusive indicators.
Define the normalization used for Table 6 and report both the cycle-compliance rate and the conditional one-pass rate while preserving the finding that replanning and goal replacement are rare.
replacements.before: Table~\ref{tab:process-dynamics} shows that one \texttt{Planning}$\rightarrow$\texttt{Translating}$\rightarrow$\texttt{Reviewing} cycle dominates the traces; returning to planning after review and replacing an existing goal are both rare.
replacements.after:
Because the trace log can omit the initial \texttt{Planning} switch, this diagnostic recovers it from the first subagent-delegation event when available and collapses immediate repetitions of the same process.
Table~\ref{tab:process-dynamics} shows that \AfourCycleCompliantRate\ of runs are cycle-compliant with the \texttt{Planning}$\rightarrow$\texttt{Translating}$\rightarrow$\texttt{Reviewing} order; \AfourCompliantOnePassRate\ of those contain one pass, while returning to planning after review and replacing an existing goal are both rare.

Unlike the normalized cycle-compliance diagnostic in Table~\ref{tab:process-dynamics}, this analysis uses the exact observed process sequence.
Table~\ref{tab:trace-outcome} compares runs that complete exactly one planning--drafting--reviewing cycle with runs that take any other path and finds similar pairwise win rates against \condFixedOrder\ and \condSingleWriter.
